# Bounded Bottleneck: `expert_bind` — Removal Plan

## 1. The Mechanism

**Root cause.** The per-token path performs 49 independent *linear walks* over the 74,391-entry mixed catalog to resolve `(buffer, offset, size)` for each routed expert. That is 49 × 74,391 ≈ 3.6 M catalog probes per token, each a name→geometry hash or sorted-scan. The catalog is **invariant** after `artifact_open()`; nothing about it changes between tokens. The per-token work is therefore pure re-derivation of a constant.

**The fix: a pre-resolved binding-descriptor table, built once at artifact-open.**

At `artifact_open()` (the point where the 74,391 tensor geometries are already parsed and the Metal buffers are already allocated), you additionally build:

```cpp
// Built ONCE, at artifact-open. Lives for the lifetime of the session.
struct ExpertBinding {
    id<MTLBuffer>  weight_buf;   // already-resolved Metal buffer
    size_t        byte_offset;  // already-resolved
    size_t        byte_size;
    // any other per-segment scalars the encoder needs
};

// Flat, dense, indexed by expert ordinal (0 … E-1).
// E = number of experts in the MoE layer (≪ 74,391; the 74k is the
// full tensor catalog across all layers/params).
std::vector<ExpertBinding> expert_binding_table;  // size E
```

Construction is a single pass over the catalog: for each tensor whose name matches the expert-weight pattern, resolve its buffer/offset/size (the work you already do today) and **store the result** into `expert_binding_table[expert_id]` instead of discarding it after the bind.

**Per-token path (replaces the walk):**

```cpp
// routed_experts: the 49 expert IDs chosen by the router this token
for (uint32_t eid : routed_experts) {
    const ExpertBinding& b = expert_binding_table[eid];   // O(1) array index
    [encoder setBuffer:b.weight_buf
               offset:b.byte_offset
               atIndex:slot_for(eid)];
}
```

49 pointer-dereferences + 49 `setBuffer` calls. No catalog walk. No hash. No scan. The 111.7 ms of host-side catalog traversal collapses to **< 0.1 ms** (49 × ~1 µs for the encoder bind, which is the irreducible Metal API cost). The GPU is no longer starved during `expert_bind`.

The table is **not** a cache that can miss. It is the catalog, re-indexed. There is no fallback path.

| `metal/metal_moe_dispatch.cpp` (or `metal/expert_bind.cpp`) | **Delete** the per-token catalog-walk loop. Replace with the 49-iteration `expert_binding_table[eid]` index + `setBuffer` loop shown above. Remove the now-dead `walk_mixed_catalog()` helper. |

If the catalog and dispatch live in a single file (common in compact Metal backends), it is one file: `metal/metal_backend.cpp`.
